Printable lesson plans

Teacher plans organised by standard, starting with 1.2. Open the complete sequence or choose an individual lesson. Every plan includes a learning intention, preparation, a timed classroom sequence, support and extension, and checks for learning.

What these resources are

Original, adaptable teaching briefs for nine standards. Each sheet contains one assessment focus, artist connections, a studio sequence, an evidence checklist and a student-friendly grade guide. These resources are independent and have not been quality assured or endorsed by NZQA.

The grade guides paraphrase the official criteria. Workload, timings and activity suggestions are teaching decisions, not NZQA thresholds or guaranteed routes to a grade. Confirm the suitability of the task and local assessment conditions before issuing it.

For the classroom: open a level overview, select a sheet and use Print / save as PDF. The print view removes navigation and leaves out teacher notes unless you select the option to include them. Print on A4 using the browser’s default margins. Artwork colour is useful but the text and grade labels also work in monochrome.

A programme, not a production line

Teach conventions and inquiry strategies, then leave room for students to choose their subject, methods and next steps. Demonstrations and formative conversations are most useful when they increase independence. Keep the assessed evidence student-led.

At Level 1, 1.2 is a substantial single resolved artwork; 1.3 focuses on developmental inquiry; 1.4 concerns a finished related series. Allow 1.2 the production scope it needs. At Levels 2 and 3, practical drawing includes painting and other visual thinking methods.

Plan integrated teaching where useful, but identify which evidence supports each standard. Do not assume completing one automatically meets another. Maintain separate, defensible judgements and normal internal moderation procedures.

External assessment conditions

For the 2026 Level 1 and Level 2 externals, NZQA excludes appropriated imagery and automatically generated content from candidate submissions. Teach with the linked artist references, but ask students to produce their own imagery and words. Level 1 conditions (PDF) · Level 2 conditions (PDF).

The 2026 Level 3 Painting rules require original thinking, acknowledgement of incorporated imagery and disclosure of generative AI use. Recognised appropriation strategies have specific conditions; they are not permission to present a copied artwork as original. These task sheets use student-generated source imagery. Level 3 conditions (PDF).

Use the studio sequences for teaching and preparation. They are not prescribed assessed response templates. During assessment, restrict conferencing, scaffolding and assistance to what NZQA permits; students must make the choices and produce the evidence. Consult the annual conditions directly, including authenticity requirements.

School verification and submission practices differ by level. See the presentation notes within each external sheet and the current NZQA Visual Arts resource hub. The 2026 format notes are reference information, not confirmation of requirements for 2027 or a later year.

Make the resource work for your class

Negotiate context, materials and scale. Use accessible water-based media where appropriate, discuss safe studio practice and follow your school procedures. Adjust teaching pace and access arrangements to students’ needs without replacing the evidence the standard requires.

Give students permission to investigate their own experiences. Work with local knowledge and relationships when engaging with culturally significant content; consult appropriate people rather than assigning motifs for decoration.

Browser notes and shared devices

Each sheet can retain optional working notes and checks in browser storage. There are no accounts, forms sent to a server or assessment uploads. On a shared device, use the clear control before leaving. Local storage can be unavailable or cleared by the browser; it is not a backup. Print or copy any notes you want to keep.

Adapting the source files

The site is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Edit the finished HTML directly, or update content.py and run python3 build.py to regenerate the pages. The print design is in dist/assets/site.css. Keep NZQA references and image credits with adapted material.

Standards & primary sources

Checked 22 November 2026. Level 1 uses the current Visual Arts standards, with painting activities. Levels 2 and 3 use the painting-specific standards. The linked older publication-year PDFs remain the referenced version 2 standards; the annual specifications are separate documents.
